points.t: A **solitary, slow-growing, red-pink, moist dome** with a collarette of scale on the **shin** of an older adult.
A benign epidermal tumour of **pale glycogen-rich keratinocytes**; possibly reactive.
**Dermoscopy**; excision or curettage for diagnosis or symptoms.
**Amelanotic melanoma**, BCC, SCC and Bowen’s look similar: biopsy if doubt.

cause.lead: Pale glycogen-filled cells in a neat plaque.
points: Cause unknown; often on legs with venous stasis or chronic inflammation.
Histology: sharply demarcated psoriasiform acanthosis of PAS-positive pale cells with intraepidermal neutrophils.

features.lead: Solitary, moist, on the lower leg.
points: **Moist red-brown dome** papule / nodule **5–20 mm** on the lower leg of a middle-aged / older adult.
Dermoscopy: dotted / glomerular vessels in a **‘string of pearls’** (necklace) arrangement: highly characteristic.

visuals.caption: Clear cell acanthoma on dermoscopy: dotted vessels lined up in curving strings like a pearl necklace (Bowen’s has clustered vessels instead).
visuals.alt: Dermoscopy circle with dotted vessels in curved strings

cards.name: Amelanotic melanoma
cards.clue: Pink lesion you can’t name confidently.

points: **Routine** referral to confirm (differential includes amelanotic melanoma and Bowen’s).
Excision, curettage or cryotherapy; recurrence uncommon.

limits.t: A solitary red scaly leg papule not responding to emollient / steroid isn’t necessarily eczema.

items.t: Pink lesion you **cannot confidently name**: exclude **amelanotic melanoma**.

pearls.t: Solitary red scaly leg papule that won’t settle → dermoscopy / biopsy, not stronger steroid.
Strings of pearls = CCA; clusters = Bowen’s.

quiz.a: Lower leg (shin) of a middle-aged / older adult.
Dotted vessels in a ‘string of pearls’ pattern.
